transcript.content: The honey badger has skin which is so thick it can withstand bee stings, porcupine quills and snake bites.

But not as good as this one. Hold on. In addition to being tough, the badger's skin is also very loose. So if it is caught by the back of the neck, that could happen, right? So you go for it, "Grr, you badger!" Back of the neck. What can it do? Nothing. Can't it? Wait a minute. It is able to twist round inside its own skin and bite whatever is holding it.
-and it, it, suddenly this skinned head comes out of its arse, bites your leg.
Well, of course it's rubbish. Who put that? I mean-
What does that mean? Its skin is so loose, it is able to twist round inside its own skin and bite whatever is holding it.
Badgers are just sort of slopping around?

What is that, a nightmare? Some sort of, um, Wesley Craven nightmares? And you've got a little badger, furry little badger, right? You think you've got it. You go, "Come on, it's for your own good." You know, you might be like Tony Soper or David Attenborough, just like, "For your own good, we're gonna go and cut your nails, pop a little thing over so we can follow you eating." But it turns round, suddenly it's a bag of skin. This head comes out of its arse-
I know! It can't be true.
A burst of static, then the recording cuts.
It was beautiful, it was a great track.
Worth, worth waiting a week for, wasn't it?
The fingerprints of a koala bear are so similar to that of a human being that if they were found at the scene of a crime, the police would not be able to tell the difference.
Is that- Well, that is the fact that I remember.
And is it, is it true?
Well... well, it depends what, what sort of crime it was, really.
You- But you got this from a reliable source?
So let me get this right. The fingerprints of a koala bear are so similar to those of a human being-
-that if they were found at the scene of a crime, the police would think that a human had committed that crime?
What kind of a crime is that?
The Great Koala Bear, um, Eucalyptus Robbery.

-they've, they've come in, right? All the, this, all the police have come in, the detectives, right? Quincy's come strolling in about half an hour later and they go, "It's all right, Quince. We've solved this one. This is obviously a human being." He goes, "Oh, is it? Oh, is it?" They go, "Well, yeah, 'course it is. There's, there's a bloke here. He's been bludgeoned to death with a lead pipe in the conservatory. He's a big lad. It's probably a six-foot bloke and he's hit him with the right hand by the window." Quincy goes, "Oh, a six-foot bloke, was it? Oh, yeah?" They go, "Yeah, well, he was-" "Oh, right. No, it's just that, you know, you've ruled out the possibility of five koala bears standing on each other's shoulders, have you?"
The bottom one's the fat one going, "Oh, where are we going?" And the top one's going, "Right, left." And they've snuck- they've gone-
They've snuck past the security guard.
They've- yeah, yeah! And they've got-
He's just, he's just said, "Go on through, sir."
Yeah. "Go on through." Yeah, it said "Press".
They've gone, "Press," right? And they've gone in there, right? And they've got this bloke, they've got his confidence. They've got a false moustache, obviously.
Right? And they go, "All right, mate." And they go, "Oh, what's that over there?"
-and the bottom one's holding it all up. Then they just scatter.
They just scatter. Dump the coat.
They just leave a coat, like an empty coat with a hat on it, right? And Quin- and, and the thing is, I think Quincy knows 'cause he's already rounded 'em up and he's got a confession out of 'em.

And so he's just being really smug. And they go, "Oh yeah, yeah, it's a bloke, innit? Yeah, it's a human being, yeah." "Well, look, Quincy, the fingerprints." "Yeah. Let's have a look at these." And they go, "D'oh!" "They're just, they're just like-" "Really?" "Yeah."
Right, and you go, "But the thing is, I think that there's a Mr Big."
He's up the tree getting stoned on eucalyptus, going, "Mmm." He's getting all the- he's counting his cash.
He's just up there hanging loose, catching it- counting his cash.
He's fingerprinted. He's got an alibi, and these pawns-
They're not gonna pin anything on Mr Big.
'Cause he's used these koala pawns in his-
Yeah. And they've done all the work. The little fat one, he's got, he's got bad shoulders now.
He's got four on him. And the tall one's got the little head with the trilby. He was at the top 'cause he can wield a, like a lead pipe, you know what I mean? Or the hat fitted him.
The hat... Have you got that letter?
Ah, yes. No, I have. No, I'm gonna, I'm gonna wait till later, actually.
There's a great letter. I'll wait till later.
Well, I'll play a song, then.
Oh, please do. But, well, be careful. I mean, if you're a police officer, if you're listening, if you're currently investigating a crime-
-you've got fingerprints, you think you've sewn it up. Think again!
Have you looked at the koala angle?
That's the first bag. So you, you seem to care about what bag it is. Is it-?
I take one from this bag.
And then I come up with a band name such as, let me see... The Riff Masters.
Nah. Do it, just do that one. Take it from any bag, yeah? Do it out of mine. Take it, any one of my bags.
All right. Um, "Axel" is the first word.
This is gonna be a cool band.
You... you just... you... I come up with great ideas. I just, you know, I come in here, I present these ideas and you just ruin them. You just take the mick.
Mm. Oh, can I just, by the way, before I do that, can I just mention that there is an email address?
Um, what show is this? How many shows have we done now? Four or five?

Anyway, there is an email address, and I'm thinking that lots of our listeners, I'm almost certain, will have access to internet email nonsense. I personally don't understand it, but if you do, then you can write to Ricky. Ricky dash Gervais at XFM dot co dot UK.
Ah. There's a- there's a bit of a drawback with email.
Do you not know how to do it?
No, I just don't, don't bother.
I, I empty my pigeonhole about once every two weeks.
Ricky dash Gervais at XFM dot co dot UK.
Here's a letter. "Dear Ricky," blah blah blah blah blah. There's a blah blah blah, "responding... Things I could do for you." Here's the important bit.
And this is, by the way, from Siobhan.
In- Siobhan in, er, Willesden. "Things I could do for you." Er... nice. This is a great idea.
Gervais, she can make you a hat. She is a professional hat maker.
Er, is it a milliner? Is that the name?
Er, but she's a professional hat maker. She can make you a hat-
-Ricky Gervais. What kind of a hat?
What would you fancy? I see you in a fez.
Oh, I know what I want.
Well, you know those top hats?
But squashed down one side, like a concertina that's made of a top hat.
What kind of a- what is that? What kind of a hat is that?

It's, it's the- it's when you- some bloke, he does philosophy for a week, or he's sort of doing French, could be, and he's- he comes in to the student union with a beret on and a goatee, and the first thing you do is take it off and throw it out the window.
Of course you do! Of course!
'Cause you're- 'cause you're with the cool people, and he's going, "Oh, that's really funny, isn't it? Yeah. So mature. Yeah." And you go, "No, it's not mature, but it's funny."
Anyone you see wearing a beret in the student union or in a pub, just pop it off. Frisbee it across the- I tell you, you will be the most popular bloke in that pub.
You see him, like, he's- he's sort of piggy in the middle. You're just throwing it, you know, to diff-
-to different people. It kind of bonds the pub.
People, they, they leave the quiz machine.
They come over and they're joining in and you're just throwing- he's screaming, "Please give me my beret back!"

In fact, I reckon if you threw it and it hit the hardest bloke in the pub's pint over, he'd look over and they'd go, "Who did that?" And I'd go, "I did, but he was wearing it." And he'd go, "Fair enough, mate." And he- d'you know what I mean?
Oh yeah. He'd go straight to the guy that was wearing the beret.
What kind of a hat- what kind of a hat is that? It's French. I mean, there's the point. That's the answer.
Oh, I- look, I don't wanna get you on French people.
No, I know, but all I would say to you is it's got no brim. You see, that can't be healthy.
What- can we get Siobhan in to measure me up for a hat?
So Siobhan, er, maybe if- if Siobhan's listening, she could give us a call.
So I could have the whole- I could have the whole suit done.
No, I was just gonna mention that she's got a friend, Catherine. She wants us to mention Catherine. Um, er, blah blah blah blah blah. Yes, Catherine's just setting up a new business. All right?
So best of luck with that, Catherine. And, um, anyway, she can make stuff for you as well.
Top hat and tails, Gervais! You would look fantastic!
We'd send you to the Ritz.
I dunno, I don't... Is that the right word? I, mm...
Oh, that would be great. You in a top hat and tails. Lovely. Lovely.
What, why does it matter which bag it is, then?
It's too complicated. Let's explain in a minute.
You've got tickets to give away, Gervais.
Yeah. Well, I've got, um, I've got to think of some questions as well.
All right, well, let's just find out what the prize is first.
Right, right. We've got, um, a pair of GusGus tickets at ULU for Friday the 13th of February.
Will you just hand them to me?
Have a look at that, yeah.
I'll just confirm that they're real.
I'm like that fella on the, um, on the lot- lottery. You know, they always go to somebody, a member of the street or somebody in a panto somewhere-
-to choose the numbers, you know. And I'm just gonna be like that, just checking.
I'll go, "Just, just check that that's a real fork. Yeah. Don't check too- Don't- You've bent it."
You've bent it, mate. You've bent the fork, mate. Now I can't do the trick. Go on.
So, two tickets to see GusGus at the University of London Union, Malet Street, London, on Friday the 13th.
Two tickets there. Yes, bona fide, Gervais.
All right, let me just check.
Two- two Cornershop tickets here, plus Les Rythmes Digitales.
This is like a real prize on our show, innit?
It is wonderful. It's wonderful. That's on Wednesday the 4th of March, again at the University of London Union. All right, two tickets there for them.
Two tickets to Catherine Wheel, mate.
To see Catherine Wheel. Again, it's at ULU. And, uh, Catherine Wheel plus special guests on Thursday the 26th of February.
So we've got the tickets there. All right, so we've got- we've got six tickets-
Right, I've got a question. I've got a question for the first one.
Good- cool name there, GusGus. Does it matter which bag they were been in?
Yeah. And I'll take any answer.
Yeah, I'll take yes or no.
I'd better remind them of the phone number.
[Jingle] Oh one seven one, five eight oh, two thousand! Call me!
I forgot- forgot I'd done that one.
So, uh, yes, two tickets for GusGus. The question again, please, Gervais?
Does it matter which bag they were in? And again it, um, it doesn't really matter. Yes or no. I'll just take anything.
All right, Catherine Wheel. You got a question for Catherine Wheel?

Catherine Wheel. Uh, yeah. When I used to do it, when- when I was little, and we used to have a Catherine wheel, my dad would nail it to the shed, set it alight. Well, the nail was way too big and tight. Know what I mean? It moved a little bit, and it just- We- what we watched was this thing just burn out.
It was more of a sort of like a-
That's all right, innit? It's not so much a question.
The question is, "That's all right, innit?" And again, I'll accept anything. Right, I'd better remind them of that number again, hold on.
Give them the- give them the number.
We've got Catherine Wheel tickets to give away-
Yeah. And the question is- not so much a question, is- what was it?
[Jingle] Oh one seven one, five eight oh, two thousand! Call me on it!
Right, so it's going- it's going well, Gervais.
GusGus, does it matter what bag it's in? The answer doesn't matter.
Um, Catherine Wheel, that's all right, innit? Right? And Cornershop.
All right, now, you've got a- now this is real- this is a gem of a prize.

Hold on, I've got- hold on one minute. I've got-

Uh... mm... [clears throat] Mm. I don't really know.
GusGus, right? Would it matter which bag they were in?
Uh, um, Catherine Wheel, that's all right, innit? Again, anything. And Cornershop...

I told- I told you they'd understand.
I must say, Gervais, that that was one of the most electrifying radio quizzes I've ever heard. Do you know what I mean? I think if we- we could option that for the telly.
We could get a whole spin-off thing going. A board game as well.
Oh, I'm- I'm- I'm thinking ahead. I'm thinking ahead.
Yeah. That is just great, Gervais. Oh man, we've just given away six tickets.
But now, your- your idea was a good one. Um, you know, all- all, um, six.
Yeah, my idea- my idea was to give away all six tickets to the first person to phone up and give us a damn good reason why they should have them.
Yeah, that's a bit traditional though, isn't it?
It's like you answer a question right and you win a prize.
But we can do yours if you want.
Okay, so I've got, um, ten CDs.
To the person who thinks why they should have all six tickets.
Well, I'm gonna give ten CDs, 'cause the tickets are gone-
-to the person with the best reason why they should have six tickets.
But they can't have the six tickets 'cause they've gone.
So they're gonna get ten CDs?
Oh. Ah, you caught me out. Hold on, one minute. One minute.
Let me just rephrase that. Basically, we've got ten CDs to give away.
If you can give us a good reason why you should have the tickets.

Old newspapers. A lot of my audience carry around bags full of, like, old newspapers going back for a long time. I've no idea why. -Gervais. Now, I know that you walk into work.

Right, we'll- we'll pass that on to Howard, we'll keep that. And, uh, as I said, anyone wants to get hold of Howard, do it via us. He doesn't really give out his address, obviously. Um, might attract mad people.
Um, now, I read in the paper years ago, um, there was this guy, right, and he was from Sheffield, and, um, uh, he was at the birth of Christ. He'd lived before as a cow.

But I just imagine people coming and saying, “I was a donkey.” “Good. Did you see it?” “No, I- there was, like, a beam in the way. I couldn't see.” “Nor could I.” “No, I was- well, I was being milked. Couldn't see a thing.” “Where were you?” “I was a chicken.” “So you saw everything?” “No, I was- I was out, wasn't I? That'd be beautiful. Yeah, no, but I- yeah, I mean, I'm sure there are all kinds of societies like this, and, uh, perhaps if you're a member of one, then we'd like to, uh, to- to, you know, find out all about you.
Two idiots talking nonsense on the radio.
